# braidpy

> A Python library for working with braids, from braid theory to the braids
> people make: by hand on a kumihimo disk, a marudai or Ashley's stand, or on
> a braiding or lace machine.

A braid is a braid word in Artin's generators. braidpy reads and writes the
common notations, works with braids (product, inverse, normal forms,
conjugacy, invariants), says which known braids one is like, draws it in the
console, in 2D and in 3D, and says how to make it by hand or on a machine.
It installs from PyPI as `braidpy`, with `braidpy[viz]` to draw and
`braidpy[mcp]` to serve an AI assistant; in the browser it is
[Braid Studio](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/studio/), with
nothing to install.

## Guides

- [Getting started](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/usage.html): a braid word, the first braids, a braid's operations.
- [Drawing braids](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/visualization.html): the console, 2D diagrams, 3D plots, animations.
- [Braid Studio](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/braid_studio.html): braidpy on a web page, how to use it.
- [Making a braid](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/making.html): from a braid word to a kumihimo disk's moves, a lace machine's punchcard, or Ashley's stand.
- [braidpy for AI assistants](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/ai_assistants.html): the front door `braidpy.tools` and the MCP server `braidpy-mcp`.
- [Glossary](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/glossary.html): the words of braiding, in braidpy's sense.
- [Reference](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/reference.html): every module, its functions and their docstrings.
- [Changelog](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/changelog.html): what changed in each release.

## How braids are written and compared

- [Braid representations](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/braid_representations.html): braid words, permutations, the Burau representation.
- [Braid algebra](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/braid_algebra.html): product, inverse, powers, normal forms.
- [Comparing braids](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/comparing_braids.html): whether two words are the same braid, and the braids most like one.

## The shape a braid takes

- [The shape of a laid rope](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/laid_rope.html): the closed form, worked through.
- [The shape of a braided tube](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/braided_tube.html): radius and clearances, in closed form.
- [Why a braid's shape has no closed form](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/why_no_closed_form.html): what stops most braids.
- [Solving a braid's shape numerically](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/solving_numerically.html): how braidpy tightens the others.

## Machines and the hand

- [Horn gear machines](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/horn_gear_layout.html): maypole machines, their gears, tracks, collisions and threading.
- [Rope physics](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/rope_physics.html): yarns that settle and tighten, as braidpy models them.
- [A marudai](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/marudai.html): a braid made move by move, round a core or not.

## Working on braidpy

- [Developer guide](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/developer_guide.html): setting up, the rules, the tests, the releases.
- [References](https://baptistelabat.github.io/braidpy/develop/references.html): the papers and books behind the mathematics.
